Method of Attack: Encrypts files on Windows systems using Elliptic-Curve Cryptography (ECC) and Salsa20 encryption
Creates multiple threads for encrypting files that do not end with .exe, .dll, or .lnk extensions
Skips files with NOKOYAWA in their names and certain directories based on hardcoded hashes
Terminates processes and services to reduce the number of locked files
Deletes volume snapshots by resizing the allocated space for snapshots of volume shadow copies
Appends a .NOKOYAWA extension to encrypted files
Creates a ransom note (NOKOYAWA_readme.txt) in every directory included for encryption
Instructs victims to contact operators via a .onion URL using the TOR browser
Impacted Systems: Files on local and networked drives
Attack Vector: Administrator privileges required for full functionality
Possible UAC bypass by operators prior to execution
Indicators of Compromise: Presence of NOKOYAWA_readme.txt files in directories
